wire.language_receipts.show_terminal.role: `/language` slash receipt printed as a notice row in the terminal and as the phone sheet's slash result — answer to bare `/language` in the terminal
wire.language_receipts.show_terminal.tone: plain, terse, lowercase command-receipt voice; no emoji
wire.language_receipts.show_terminal.note: EN-only context sidecar. Terminal form: the value space is NOT enumerated because the terminal has a space-key picker. `/language <value>` is the literal command and stays verbatim; `space` names the key that opens the picker. {tag} / {key} are locale tags or the word `auto` (technical tokens: keep them verbatim, never translate or transliterate). {name} is the language's OWN native name (for example `Français`), already localized data: do not translate it. Must fit the 70-cell notice row at 80 columns.

wire.language_receipts.show_options.role: `/language` slash receipt printed as a notice row in the terminal and as the phone sheet's slash result — answer to bare `/language` on the phone sheet
wire.language_receipts.show_options.tone: plain, terse, lowercase command-receipt voice; no emoji
wire.language_receipts.show_options.note: EN-only context sidecar. Phone form: the sheet has no argument picker, so {options} is the comma-separated list of accepted values (`auto` plus shipped locale tags): technical tokens, keep verbatim. {tag} / {key} are locale tags or the word `auto` (technical tokens: keep them verbatim, never translate or transliterate). {name} is the language's OWN native name (for example `Français`), already localized data: do not translate it.

wire.language_receipts.unknown_terminal.role: `/language` slash receipt printed as a notice row in the terminal and as the phone sheet's slash result — refusal of an unrecognised value in the terminal
wire.language_receipts.unknown_terminal.note: EN-only context sidecar. {echo} is the value the user typed, already clipped to fit the row and quoted: keep it verbatim. `space` names the key that lists the values.

wire.language_receipts.unknown_options.role: `/language` slash receipt printed as a notice row in the terminal and as the phone sheet's slash result — refusal of an unrecognised value on the phone sheet
wire.language_receipts.unknown_options.note: EN-only context sidecar. {echo} is the user's clipped, quoted input (verbatim). {options} is the comma-separated list of accepted values (technical tokens, verbatim).

wire.language_receipts.already.role: `/language` slash receipt printed as a notice row in the terminal and as the phone sheet's slash result — no-op when the requested value is already stored
wire.language_receipts.already.tone: plain, terse, lowercase command-receipt voice; no emoji
wire.language_receipts.already.note: EN-only context sidecar. Said when `/language <value>` names the value already saved; {tag} is what that value resolves to on this machine (with `auto` it comes from the environment, then the OS). {tag} / {key} are locale tags or the word `auto` (technical tokens: keep them verbatim, never translate or transliterate). {name} is the language's OWN native name (for example `Français`), already localized data: do not translate it.

wire.language_receipts.unregistered.role: `/language` slash receipt printed as a notice row in the terminal and as the phone sheet's slash result — guard for a broken build
wire.language_receipts.unregistered.note: EN-only context sidecar. Developer-facing guard that should never show to a user; keep short. No ICU arguments.

wire.language_receipts.save_failed.role: `/language` slash receipt printed as a notice row in the terminal and as the phone sheet's slash result — the config write failed
wire.language_receipts.save_failed.note: EN-only context sidecar. {key} is the value that could not be saved (tag or `auto`, verbatim). {error} is a short English system reason from the config layer and is NOT translated; place it last.

wire.language_receipts.saved.role: `/language` slash receipt printed as a notice row in the terminal and as the phone sheet's slash result — success receipt after switching
wire.language_receipts.saved.tone: plain, terse, lowercase command-receipt voice; no emoji
wire.language_receipts.saved.note: EN-only context sidecar. Printed once, in the NEW language, right after the switch: {key} is what was saved (`auto` or a tag), {tag}/{name} is the language now active. {tag} / {key} are locale tags or the word `auto` (technical tokens: keep them verbatim, never translate or transliterate). {name} is the language's OWN native name (for example `Français`), already localized data: do not translate it.
